subject: Geopolitics
title: Propaganda and Disinformation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Propaganda and Disinformation.

hook.text: Russia's Internet Research Agency employed 1,000 people to post fake content targeting American voters full-time.

buildup.text: Disinformation creates false narratives. Propaganda amplifies real grievances. Both are tools of covert influence.

discovery.text: The goal isn't to convince but to confuse. When nobody trusts anything, authoritarian narratives fill the vacuum.

twist.text: Democracies are vulnerable because free speech protects lies alongside truth.

climax.text: AI-generated deepfakes make disinformation cheaper and more convincing. The arms race between fake and detection is on.

punchline.text: Truth is slow. Lies travel at the speed of a click.

quiz.question: Why are democracies especially vulnerable to disinformation?
options: Democracies lack intelligence agencies to counter it
Free speech protections make it hard to restrict false content
Democratic citizens are less educated on average
